bullets.title: UBS Tech Musings: Semis bullish, ORCL capex concern, NVDA/MRVL/AMD ranked; ADBE AI deflationary
bullets.body: UBS's weekly tech sentiment flags SOX +9.4% with bullish bias on MU upside, and a clear compute preference hierarchy: NVDA > MRVL > AMD > ARM > AVGO. AVGO faces headwinds from V9 packaging (EMIB availability) and Mediatek share gains at Google/TPU. INTC improved on foundry narrative but EPS power limited at $5-7/share. ADBE is shifting to freemium as AI deflates software pricing, and ORCL commentary on peak FY28 capex drew investor concern. PLTR named top pick for rerating followed by SNOW and DDOG.

bullets.title: ADBE crashes on CFO exit, organic ARR cut ~$500M; multiple downgrades
bullets.body: Adobe's Q2 beat headlines but organic ARR guidance was cut ~$500M as the company pivots to freemium and defers Creative Cloud optimizations. CFO Dan Durn is departing to Marvell (effective June 15), leaving Adobe without CEO or CFO. Wolfe downgraded to Peer Perform (fair value $165-210), Evercore to in-line (PT $225), Stifel to hold (PT $200), and Freedom Broker to hold. DA Davidson maintains Buy with noise in F2H26. Stock hit 52-week lows, now trading at ~8-10x CY27 GAAP P/E vs. peer median 24x.

bullets.title: ORCL beats Q4 but $90-95B FY27 capex and $40B capital raise weigh on stock
bullets.body: Oracle reported Q4 EPS $2.11 vs $1.96 est and revenue $19.18B. RPO surged to $638B (+363% YoY) including $75B in customer prepaid/BYOH contracts. FY27 guidance reaffirmed at $90B revenue and $8.05 EPS. However, net cash capex of ~$70B plus plans to raise ~$40B in debt/equity in FY27 (including $20B ATM issuance) prompted a ~10% post-earnings drop. Citi maintains Buy $330 PT; Mizuho Outperform; UBS Buy $285; Wolfe raised PT to $225. Bears note negative FCF of -$23.7B and margin compression risk.

bullets.title: AMD upgraded to Buy at Citi and others on Meta GPU deal; $575 PT; CPU TAM expansion
bullets.body: Citi upgraded AMD from Hold to Buy (PT $575 from $460) citing emergence as legitimate GPU second source—AMD is positioned to win lion's share of Meta's ~6 GW, 4-year custom MI450 deal worth ~$15B/GW. CY26/27/28 EPS estimates revised 12-13% above Street consensus. AI sales expected to reach $33B in 2027 (up 137% YoY) and $50.8B in 2028. CPU TAM expanded to $137B by 2030 (36% CAGR). Truist also upgraded AMD based on industry checks; AMD now leads Amazon's CPU best-seller chart with 15 of 15 positions vs. zero for INTC.

bullets.title: INTC double-upgraded to Buy at BofA ($135 PT) on foundry opportunity and CPU TAM expansion
bullets.body: Bank of America double-upgraded Intel from Underperform to Buy, raising PT to $135 from $96, citing leading-edge wafer and packaging opportunities including EMIB and the GOOGL TPU chip deal. INTC surged 25%+ on the week (+237% YTD per S&P weekly data). BofA also raised CPU TAM forecast to $170B+ by 2030 from $125B, citing agentic AI demand for ARM, AMD, INTC.

bullets.title: ROKU in acquisition talks; MS Overweight on new home screen; PSKY double-upgraded
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Roku is in talks to sell itself to at least one US media company; stock surged ~$25 to ~$144.64 (+20%). Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight on Roku's new home screen. PSKY (Paramount Skydance) was double-upgraded to Overweight at Morgan Stanley. DOJ approved the Paramount/Skydance/WBD deal without conditions; California AG Rob Bonta could still sue to block.

bullets.title: Mag 7 recap: MSFT Xbox layoffs, META Manus unwind, GOOGL AI investments, AMZN $17.5B loan
bullets.body: Key Mag 7 developments this week: MSFT Xbox plans major layoffs post-June 30 fiscal year-end, stock fell ~6.2% on week; META unwound its $2B Manus acquisition due to Chinese regulatory opposition; GOOGL raised $80B+ via equity and received $35B Anthropic chip financing backstop; AMZN secured $17.5B delayed draw term loan for AI capex, also issued largest-ever Canadian bond deal; NVDA's Vera AI CPU available in China by August with NVDA denying 800V/CPO delays from SemiAnalysis.

bullets.title: AVGO: $35B AI XPV platform with Apollo/Blackstone; 20GW target; $130-190B revenue potential by 2028
bullets.body: Broadcom anchors a $35B AI infrastructure SPV with Apollo, Blackstone, KIA, and NVDA targeting 20GW of compute for Anthropic and OpenAI through CY28. UBS reiterates Buy $485 PT; purchase commitments jumped to $128B in F2Q26 from $54B prior quarter. Revenue per GW reiterated at $10-15B. Key gating factors: data center shell availability and software stack readiness. At 13GW shipments in CY28, potential $130-190B in revenue.

bullets.title: MU: Wolfe raises PT to $1,250; LTAs locking 2028 supply; CSPs now securing HBM4
bullets.body: Wolfe Research raised MU price target to $1,250 from $550 as CSPs move to secure 2028 LTA memory capacity after locking 2027. DRAM ASP rising 35% q/q in C2Q following 75% in Q1; another +15% forecast in Q3. CY27 HBM pricing up 40% YoY driven by HBM4 adoption. Wolfe models CY27 MU revenue at $226B and EPS $135 vs. Street at $186B/$107. MU stock trades below 6x forward EPS. Jensen Huang confirmed SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron all certified on HBM4 for Vera Rubin.

bullets.title: DKNG: CEO confirms no OSB cannibalization from prediction markets; +24% revenue
bullets.body: DraftKings reported net revenue +24% YoY with sportsbook revenue +30%. CEO at Jefferies conference confirmed prediction markets are incremental with no material OSB cannibalization—professional sharps moving to PMs improves hold economics. Prediction market handle growing 34% m/m to $3.1B annualized in May. CFTC proposed lenient prediction market rules, fueling +15% 2-day rally. Jefferies turned incrementally bullish noting PMs double TAM without proportional marketing spend.

bullets.title: ANET: PT raised to $190 at MS and JPM on front-end AI networking TAM expansion
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised Arista PT to $190 (from $180) and Cisco to $130, citing front-end network refresh driven by rising CPU intensity in agentic AI. ANET launched 1.6T rack-scale portfolio (one product in Q4 2026, two in Q1 2027) collaborating with META, MSFT, and ORCL. Dell'Oro estimates AI front-end networking spend grows from ~$1.8B (2025) to ~$6.3B (2030) at 29% CAGR; MS bull case $10B. AI agents generate 450% more traffic than humans. Cisco target now $130 on AI pipeline visibility.

bullets.title: HOOD: Director buys $55M in stock; platform assets +48% YoY; underwriter approval
bullets.body: Robinhood director Meyer Malka purchased $55.3M in shares over 7 days. Platform assets hit $377B (+48% YoY) with May net deposits of $5.6B. HOOD received regulatory approval to serve as IPO underwriter. Needham raised PT to $97. Prediction market annualized volumes surging; Mizuho raised PT to $115 modeling 44.8B contracts in FY26.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: CPO delay overhang; LITE CEO confirms guidance beat pace; NVDA denies pushouts
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis report on CPO timeline pushed to 2028-29 for scale-up triggered a broad optical selloff. However, LITE CEO Michael Hurlston at Mizuho conference confirmed the company is on pace to meet/exceed the top end of guidance, scale-up CPO products shipping H2 2027 with formal ramp in 2028, and NPO opportunity could be 'frankly bigger than CPO.' NVDA SVP also denied CPO/800V delays, and Morgan Stanley defended the optical thesis noting CPO content grows regardless of timing. JPM reiterates OW on COHR and LITE.

bullets.title: GEV: Morgan Stanley sees gas turbine orders declining in 2027; ETN/DAN RMT deal
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes its model still calls for gas turbine industry orders to decrease in 2027 vs. 2026 levels of ~117GW. Separately, Eaton (ETN) announced a Reverse Morris Trust merger combining its Mobility Group with Dana; ETN owns 50.1%+ and receives $1.1B cash distribution. ROK had upbeat discussions on AI integration, short-cycle recovery, and margin expansion.

bullets.title: TSLA: SpaceX/Tesla merger at 80% probability for 2027 per CNBC; GLJ maintains Sell $24.86
bullets.body: Multiple sources on CNBC cited an 80% probability of SpaceX/Tesla merger by 2027, which would be a transformative catalyst. Elon's Tesla AI6 chip may achieve record usable intelligence per wafer per Tesla's engineering team. Separately, GLJ Research maintained its Sell rating ($24.86 PT), citing inventory clearing and seasonal demand masking underlying weakness.

bullets.title: RH: Q1 beat but Q2 guidance soft; FY 4.5-8% growth hinges on unproven Estates launch
bullets.body: Restoration Hardware reported Q1 EPS loss better than expected with revenue and margins above consensus. Q2 revenue guidance +0.5-2.5% missed consensus of +4.6%. FY26 revenue guidance 4.5-8.0% midpoint slightly ahead. RH Estates launch targeted for fall 2026 will represent 60-65% of business; management says 5% of H2 growth depends on it. Multiple banks cautious: Citi Neutral $166 PT; UBS Neutral $40; Morgan Stanley OW $240 on operating leverage thesis.

bullets.title: CHWY: Q1 beat but FY guidance cut $200M; active customers disappoint
bullets.body: Chewy Q1 EBITDA beat consensus ($253M vs $242M est) but lowered FY26 net sales guidance by ~$200M to $13.40-13.55B, citing macro pressure and reduced premiumization attach. Active customer net adds missed at 170K vs. 270K expected. MoffettNathanson downgraded to Neutral with PT cut 56% to $22. JPM cut PT to $29 but maintained Overweight citing durable margin expansion and 2x+ industry growth rate.

bullets.title: SPOT: Citi Buy $620 PT after Investor Day; Audiobooks+ at €100M ARR; Marketplace 4x growth
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy $620 PT on Spotify after Investor Day clarifications. Marketplace grew 4x from 2021-2025, contributing ~50% of Premium gross margin expansion. Audiobooks+ on track for €100M ARR by July 2026 with 1M subs. KeyBanc survey shows 53% of Spotify listeners canceling intent lowest for second consecutive quarter. Model changes small (<1%) but positive.

bullets.title: ETSY: JPM raises PT to $78 on AI-driven GMS growth; agentic commerce positioning
bullets.body: JPM raised ETSY December 2026 PT to $78 (from $75) following Brooklyn HQ management access. App GMS accelerating to +11% YoY in Q1 vs +7% in Q4. App users maintain 40% higher LTV profiles. Agentic commerce could surface long-tail inventory from Etsy's 2.5B listings base. Morgan Stanley sees medium-term upside but long-term risk from AI horizontal agents; bull case models 29%/40% GMS/EBITDA upside vs base. Jefferies maintains Hold $62 PT.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi maintains Buy after CFO meeting; AIP traction despite bookings softness from Middle East conflict
bullets.body: Citi reiterates PLTR Buy ($225 PT, 71.7% upside) after CFO Glazer meeting. Q1 weaker bookings attributed to Middle East conflict redirecting USG resources; expects normalization in Q2. Continued AIP traction with NHS wins and new verticals. Palantir launching token optimization and security tools, targeting Rule-of-100+ metrics. Positioned at center of enterprise AI cost-control via Foundry/AIP model routing. Morgan Stanley identifies PLTR as top pick for software rerating.
